s: The Devil exalts himself against his Creator. God tells him that those he cannot deceive will inherit his throne, and he will burn in Gehenna for ever.
The Devil boasts that he will lead all the sons of Adam astray. God reminds him of Job, whom he could not deceive, and of why he fell from among the archangels.
God gave Adam both good and evil thoughts. When Adam sinned he was sent out of Paradise, yet God still feeds him from the earth.
God promises to redeem Adam and to put the Devil to shame. Those who keep his law will praise him with the holy angels.
Remember your Creator who made you from the earth. Do not lie or deceive your neighbour, and do not be proud.
Remember the day of your death and the dreadful angels who will come for sinners. Live simply and treat your servants justly.
Those who trust in God have no fear. Care for the widow and the orphan, and God will protect your children.
Job trusted in God and was saved from all his trials. Trust God and he will be your refuge.
All creation obeys its Creator. Turn from sin before God's judgment, when all will receive what their deeds deserve.
As the seeds and creatures rise again in spring, so the dead will rise. Share with the poor and believe in the resurrection, to rejoice in the kingdom of heaven.
i: 3 Meqabyan, the last and shortest of the three Ethiopian books of Meqabyan, is almost entirely teaching. It opens with a conversation between the Devil and God, and develops the old tradition that Satan fell because he refused to bow before Adam.

Its great theme is the resurrection of the body. It gathers examples from Israel’s history and from nature, the seed that dies and rises, to show that the dead will live again and stand before God’s judgment, and it calls the reader to repentance before that day.
What to expect: ten chapters of sermons rather than a story. The Catholic Church does not count it among the books of the Bible.
